items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: like Procope. He's still living and playing very well. But you don't hear anything about it.

ctx.x: And my feelings are that we are going to have to join together and to be motivated and to do some of these things just as the...you take Billy Taylor. Billy Taylor has done one hell of a job for modern jazz. He's been in on all of the committees,

you know what I mean, he's been where the, you know, where the money's allocated and appropriated and where the plans are formulated...he's been in on all of that. So as a result of that, his Jazzmobile has been a success.

You have very few older musicians playing on the darn thing, so I think that simultaneously with that...I don't say to cut it out...I say but add more to another facet so that you've got maybe thirty concerts underwritten by the city with the union and thirty different public places, where the jazz musicians can come...the best can come and play and be presented and to make the world aware that a lot of these great guys...like Procope. He's still living and playing very well. But you don't hear anything about it.…
